summary: All three TDD-anchor tests from task 6 are present, named exactly as required, and probe real behaviour. The suite is plain JUnit 5 with no Spring context, instantiating NoOpSubscriberService directly — fast and isolated. StepVerifier.expectComplete().verify(Duration.ofMillis(100)) is the right shape for an in-memory Mono.empty() call: a null return would NPE inside StepVerifier.create, a non-empty/non-completing Mono would time out, and adding a null-check on optional fields would throw before StepVerifier ever runs. All three tests pass the litmus test — removing the Mono.empty() body of either impl method causes failures. For a deliberately minimal stub shim, coverage is adequate; no extra cases warranted beyond the three anchors.
